blocks.text: Yeh chapter 28 (Chromatography) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 4 number ka hai (wazahat, equations, zaroorat ho to diagram), aur chapter ke numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain. Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 What is chromatography? Explain why it is needed for complex mixtures, what it allows chemists to do, and name its three important types. Also define adsorption with an example. (4 marks)
(Chromatography kya hai? Wazahat karein ke complex mixtures ke liye is ki zaroorat kyun hai, is se chemists kya kar sakte hain, aur is ki teen ahem qismein batayein. Adsorption ki tareef misaal ke saath bhi karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Zaroorat: simple mixture se aik do components filtration, distillation aur solvent extraction jaisi simple techniques se alag ho jate hain, lekin complex mixtures ke liye advanced techniques chahiye.

Chromatography: aik versatile (har fun) aur ahem analytical technique jo complex mixture ke components ko do mukhtalif phases (stationary aur mobile) ke liye un ki mukhtalif affinity (kashish) ki buniyad par alag karti hai. Misaalein: phoolon ke dyes, paani mein pollutants, patton se dawai ke extracts (maslan patton ke pigments).

Faide: is se substances ki identification (pehchan), purification (safai) aur quantification (miqdaar) bohat durustgi se hoti hai, is liye yeh medicine, forensic aur environmental science mein jadeed analytical tool hai.

Teen ahem qismein: paper chromatography (PC), thin layer chromatography (TLC) aur gas chromatography (GC).

Adsorption: satah ka amal (surface phenomenon) jis mein zarre sirf bahar ki satah par jama hote hain. Misaal: activated charcoal gases aur impurities ko apni satah par adsorb karta hai, is liye filters aur purification systems mein istemal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Chromatography is a versatile and important analytical technique

blocks.prompt:
2 Explain the roles of the stationary phase and the mobile phase in paper chromatography. What is the Rf value? Give its formula and explain why it has no unit and when it stays constant. (4 marks)
(Paper chromatography mein stationary phase aur mobile phase ka kirdar wazeh karein. Rf value kya hai? Is ka formula dein aur batayein ke is ka unit kyun nahi aur yeh kab qaim rehti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Stationary phase: paper mein cellulose ke saath juda paani hota hai; yehi phansa hua paani stationary phase hai.
Mobile phase: solvent, jo paper mein upar charhta hai aur sample ke spot se guzarta hai (solvent ki satah spot se neeche rakhi jati hai).

Separation: sample ke solutes dono phases mein mukhtalif had tak hal hote hain. Jo solvent (mobile phase) mein ziyada hal hon woh paper par upar jate hain; jo paper ke paani (stationary phase) mein ziyada hal hon woh door nahi jate. Hal-pazeeri ka yeh farq unhein alag karta hai; usool relative solubility (partition) hai.

Rf value (retardation ya retention factor):
Rf = substance ka tay kiya faasla / solvent ka tay kiya faasla
• Rf ka koi unit nahi kyun ke yeh do faaslon ki ratio hai.
• Same solvent aur same temperature par kisi substance ki Rf value nahi badalti, is liye is se substance pehchana ja sakta hai.

book_ref.quote: This difference in the solubility allows the different components in the sample to be separated.

blocks.prompt:
3 A mixture of two dyes is run on paper. The solvent front is 8.0 cm from the baseline. Dye P is at 2.4 cm and dye Q at 5.6 cm. (i) Calculate the Rf value of each dye. (ii) Which dye is more soluble in the water of the paper? (iii) Where would a dye of Rf 0.45 appear on a paper whose solvent front is 6.0 cm? (4 marks)
(Do dyes ka mixture paper par chalaya gaya. Solvent front baseline se 8.0 cm par hai. Dye P 2.4 cm aur dye Q 5.6 cm par hai. (i) Har dye ki Rf nikalein. (ii) Kaun si dye paper ke paani mein ziyada hal hoti hai? (iii) Rf 0.45 wali dye 6.0 cm solvent front wale paper par kahan aaye gi?)
blocks.explanation: Har spot ke faasle ko solvent ke faasle se taqseem karein; kam chalne wali dye stationary paani mein ziyada rehti hai; (iii) mein Rf ko solvent ke faasle se zarb dein.

book_ref.quote: is calculated by dividing the distance traveled by the component with the distance travelled by the solvent.

steps: Rf = substance ka faasla / solvent ka faasla
P kam chalti hai (Rf kam), is liye yeh paper ke phanse paani (stationary phase) mein ziyada hal hoti hai.
(iii) faasla = Rf × solvent ka faasla = 0.45 × 6.0 cm = 2.7 cm
blocks.final_answer: Rf(P) = 0.30, Rf(Q) = 0.70; P paper ke paani mein ziyada hal hoti hai; Rf 0.45 wali dye baseline se 2.7 cm par aaye gi.

blocks.prompt:
4 Describe how a TLC plate is prepared and how the samples are spotted and run. How are colourless components made visible? (4 marks)
(Batayein ke TLC plate kaise tayyar hoti hai aur samples kaise lagaye aur chalaye jate hain. Be-rang components ko kaise nazar aane wala banaya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Plate ki tayyari: alumina (Al₂O₃) ya silica (SiO₂) ko paani mein mila kar slurry banti hai jo glass slide par barabar phailayi jati hai. Layer ko oven mein sukha kar safed solid layer banti hai, yehi stationary phase hai.

Spot lagana aur chalana:
• Slide ke neeche ke qareeb pencil aur ruler se seedhi baseline kheenchi jati hai.
• Capillary tube se baseline par sample ka spot lagaya jata hai; aik hi slide par mukhtalif jagahon par kayi samples lag sakte hain.
• Solvent (mobile phase) chromatography tank mein liya jata hai aur slide aise dubayi jati hai ke baseline solvent se upar rahe.
• Solvent kuch oonchai tak charh jaye to slide nikali jati hai, solvent front mark hota hai aur slide dryer se sukhayi jati hai.

Be-rang components (locating agents):
• Ninhydrin spray be-rang amino acids ko purple (jamni) karta hai.
• Kuch be-rang substances ultra-violet light mein chamakte hain.
• Kuch iodine vapours se bhoore ho jate hain.

book_ref.quote: In thin layer chromatography (TLC), alumina (Al₂O₃) or silica (SiO₂) is mixed in water to make slurry

blocks.prompt:
5 Explain how the polarity of substances decides how far they travel in TLC, and how the separated components are finally identified. (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke TLC mein substances ki polarity kaise tay karti hai ke woh kitna door jayenge, aur alag huay components ki aakhir mein pehchan kaise hoti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Do amal saath chalte hain: components solvent (mobile phase) mein hal hote hain aur aluminium oxide (stationary phase) par mukhtalif had tak adsorb hote hain.

• Polar substances polar solid stationary phase ki taraf ziyada khinchte hain aur mazbooti se adsorb hote hain, is liye slide par ahista charhte hain (Rf kam).
• Non-polar substances non-polar solvent mein ziyada hal hote hain, is liye slide par ziyada upar jate hain (Rf ziyada).
Adsorption aur solubility ka yeh farq substances ko alag karta hai (usool: adsorption + solubility).

Pehchan: run ke baad solvent front mark kar ke slide sukhayi jati hai. Har spot ki Rf (spot ka faasla / solvent ka faasla) nikal kar standard values se milayi jati hai; milti Rf values components ki pehchan karti hain. Be-rang spots pehle locating agent (ninhydrin, UV light ya iodine vapours) se nazar aane wale banaye jate hain.

book_ref.quote: This difference allows the substances in the sample to separate.

blocks.prompt:
6 A sample is run on a TLC slide. The solvent front is 6.0 cm from the baseline and two spots appear at 1.5 cm and 4.5 cm. In the same solvent and temperature, standard Rf values are: X = 0.25, Y = 0.50, Z = 0.75. (i) Calculate the Rf of both spots. (ii) Identify the components. (iii) Which component is more polar if the stationary phase is polar? (4 marks)
(Aik sample TLC slide par chalaya gaya. Solvent front baseline se 6.0 cm par hai aur do spots 1.5 cm aur 4.5 cm par hain. Usi solvent aur temperature par standard Rf values: X = 0.25, Y = 0.50, Z = 0.75. (i) Dono spots ki Rf nikalein. (ii) Components pehchanein. (iii) Polar stationary phase par kaun sa component ziyada polar hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har Rf nikal kar standard list se milayein (halaat same hain is liye theek hai), aur yaad rakhein ke ziyada polar substance ziyada ruk jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Rf values of different coloured spots are calculated.

steps: Rf = spot ka faasla / solvent front ka faasla
Spot 1: Rf = 1.5 cm / 6.0 cm = 0.25 → X se milta hai
Spot 2: Rf = 4.5 cm / 6.0 cm = 0.75 → Z se milta hai
Same solvent aur temperature par Rf nahi badalti, is liye yeh milaan durust hai.
X (Rf 0.25) polar stationary phase par ziyada rukta hai, is liye X ziyada polar hai.
blocks.final_answer: Rf = 0.25 (X) aur 0.75 (Z); sample mein X aur Z hain; X ziyada polar hai.

blocks.prompt:
7 Describe the applications of thin layer chromatography. (4 marks)
(Thin layer chromatography ki applications (istemal) bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
1. Pehchan: TLC na-maloom compounds ki Rf values standard values se mila kar un ki pehchan karti hai.
2. Purity: kisi substance ki purity (khalis-pan) TLC se check hoti hai.
3. Reaction ki progress: TLC batati hai ke reactants khatam ho rahe hain ya products ban rahe hain.
4. Pharmaceutical aur food industry: drugs ki purity aur khanay mein preservatives, colourants aur sweeteners ki maujoodgi check hoti hai.
5. Mahol: TLC mitti, paani, khanay aur hawa mein pollutants, pesticides aur zehreele substances ka pata lagati hai.
6. Forensic science: jurm ki jagah par drugs, dhamakay ka malba, khoon, paseena aur semen pehchanti hai.

book_ref.quote: In pharmaceutical and food industry, purity of drugs and presence of preservatives

blocks.prompt:
8 Explain the limitations of thin layer chromatography. (4 marks)
(Thin layer chromatography ki limitations (hudood) wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
1. Zyada tar qualitative: TLC substance ki miqdaar ka sirf andaza deti hai, is liye durust aur precise quantitative technique nahi.
2. Qareebi Rf par kamzor resolution: qareebi Rf values wale compounds saaf alag nahi hote, is liye spots hamesha saaf nahi hote.
3. Sirf chhota paimana: sirf thori miqdaar ka sample lagaya aur analyse kiya ja sakta hai, is liye bari miqdaar ki separation ke liye munasib nahi.
4. Kam reproducibility: yeh technique nami (humidity), temperature aur kaam ki jagah ki safai ke liye hassaas hai, jis se dobara wohi nateeja aana kam hota hai.

book_ref.quote: In TLC, only small amounts of sample can be applied and analysed.

blocks.prompt:
9 Explain how the components of a mixture are separated inside the column of a gas chromatograph. What are retention time and a chromatogram? (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke gas chromatograph ke column ke andar mixture ke components kaise alag hote hain. Retention time aur chromatogram kya hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Phases: stationary phase silica (SiO₂) ya alumina (Al₂O₃) ke chhote zarron par juda non-volatile, long-chain, non-polar hydrocarbon liquid hai jis ka boiling point ziyada hai; mobile phase helium ya nitrogen jaisi inert carrier gas hai.

Separation: bukhaar bana sample carrier gas ke saath lambe coiled column se guzarta hai jo bare surface area wale chhote silica zarron se bhara hai; inhi par separation hoti hai. Non-polar substances stationary phase ke non-polar liquid se ziyada interact karte hain, is liye column mein ahista chalte hain. Ziyada interact karne wale ahista aur baaqi tez chalte hain, yun woh alag ho jate hain (usool: gas-liquid partition).

Chromatogram: column se nikalte alag shuda substances detector se guzarte hain jo unhein pehchan kar chromatogram naam ke graph par peaks ki shakal mein record karta hai.

Retention time: kisi substance ko column se guzarne mein lagne wala waqt; detector har component ka yeh waqt record karta hai.

book_ref.quote: The non-polar substances in the mixture have greater interaction with non-polar liquid

blocks.prompt:
10 Explain how gas chromatography is used as a quantitative technique to find the composition of a mixture of three esters A, B and C. When is peak height used instead of peak area? (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke teen esters A, B aur C ke mixture ki composition maloom karne ke liye gas chromatography quantitative technique ke tor par kaise istemal hoti hai. Peak area ki bajaye peak height kab istemal hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
GC mein ziyada sensitivity, achi resolution, tez analysis aur durust miqdaar hai; yeh quantitative (miqdaari) technique hai.

1. Pehle chromatogram ki peaks pehchani jati hain (har component ki apni peak hoti hai).
2. Har peak ka area naapa jata hai. Peaks triangle jaisi hain, is liye:
   Peak ka area = ½ × base × height
3. Har peak ka area us component ka hissa batata hai:
   A ki % = A ki peak ka area / (A, B aur C ki peaks ke areas ka jama) × 100
   isi tarah B aur C ke liye.

Peak height: agar peaks bohat tang hon ya un ki base width milti julti ho to area ki bajaye peak height se components ka hissa andaza kiya jata hai.

book_ref.quote: GC is also a quantitative technique.

blocks.prompt:
11 A mixture of three esters A, B and C gives a gas chromatogram with triangular peaks: A (base 2.0 mm, height 6.0 mm), B (base 2.0 mm, height 9.0 mm), C (base 3.0 mm, height 10.0 mm). Calculate the percentage of each ester in the mixture. (4 marks)
(Teen esters A, B aur C ke mixture se triangle jaisi peaks wala gas chromatogram mila: A (base 2.0 mm, height 6.0 mm), B (base 2.0 mm, height 9.0 mm), C (base 3.0 mm, height 10.0 mm). Mixture mein har ester ki percentage nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Har peak ka area ½ × base × height se nikalein, sab jama karein, phir har area ko kul ki percentage mein likhein.

book_ref.quote: The peaks are similar to triangles, therefore, the area of peak can be calculated by the following formula.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Yahan C ki height sab se ziyada hai lekin is ki base bhi chauri hai, is liye height ki bajaye area istemal kiya: base widths milti julti nahi hain.

blocks.prompt:
12 Describe the applications of gas chromatography in industry, forensic science, the food industry, clinical work and sports. (4 marks)
(Gas chromatography ki applications industry, forensic science, food industry, clinical kaam aur khel mein bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
1. Industry: GC quality control aur mahol ki hifazat ke liye ahem hai; petrochemical plants is se fuels ki composition dekhte hain aur environmental samples mein organic pollutants ki bohat thori miqdaar ka pata lagate hain.
2. Forensic science: is se aksar blood alcohol content (BAC) test hote hain aur biological samples mein ghair qanooni drugs, zeher ya performance barhane wale substances ka pata chalta hai. (Misaal: Nian Bin case mein khanay ka GC test hua jis ne sabit kiya ke zeher nahi mila tha.)
3. Food aur beverage industry: products ki yaksaaniyat aur hifazat; bacteria ya fungi ke metabolic byproducts pehchan kar kharabi ka nazar aane se pehle pata, aur perfumes, essential oils aur flavourings ki khushbu ka analysis.
4. Clinical aur pharmaceutical: mareez ki saans ya urine ke compounds se metabolic bimariyon ki tashkhees, aur naye drugs ki purity test taa ke koi nuqsaan-deh bacha solvent ya impurity na rahe.
5. Khel: khiladiyon mein steroids ki maujoodgi aur car racing ke fuel ke components ka test.

book_ref.quote: In the industrial sector, GC is vital for quality control and environmental protection.

blocks.prompt:
13 State the advantages and the limitations of gas chromatography. (4 marks)
(Gas chromatography ke faide aur limitations (hudood) bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Faide:
• Ziyada sensitivity, achi resolution, tez analysis aur durust miqdaar.
• Gases ka mixture room temperature par aasani se alag ho jata hai.
• Yeh quantitative technique hai: peak areas har component ka hissa batate hain.

Limitations:
1. GC sirf volatile (aasani se bukhaar banne wale) substances ke liye kaam karti hai.
2. Samples thermally stable (garmi par qaim) hone chahiye; tez garmi se toot jane wale compounds istemal nahi ho sakte.
3. Proteins aur polymers jaise bare biomolecules analyse nahi ho sakte kyun ke aasani se bukhaar nahi bante.
4. GC ke instruments aur maintenance ka kharcha ziyada hai.

book_ref.quote: GC works only for volatile (easily vaporised) substances.

blocks.prompt:
14 Compare paper chromatography, thin layer chromatography and gas chromatography with respect to principle, mobile phase, stationary phase and speed. (4 marks)
(Paper chromatography, thin layer chromatography aur gas chromatography ka muqabla usool, mobile phase, stationary phase aur raftaar ke lehaz se karein.)
blocks.explanation: Teeno qismon ka muqabla table mein hai. Paper chromatography solvent aur paper ke paani ke darmiyan relative solubility se alag karti hai; TLC silica/alumina par adsorption aur solvent mein solubility se; GC carrier gas aur coiled column ke non-volatile liquid ke darmiyan partition se.

book_ref.quote: Comparison of three types of chromatography
